summary: Enterprise Suite AC-17 adds a local auth runtime foundation for later cloud gateway integration. It validates tenant-bound issuer/audience/nonce/session claims, deny-by-default route scopes across the 19-route local HR/Payroll/Accounting/Enterprise Suite catalog, sensitive-data MFA/AAL2 requirements, break-glass audit requirements, and cloud-readiness-gate composition while keeping external OIDC/JWKS/provider verification and deployed gateway enforcement as explicit non-claims.

findings: The auth runtime is a deterministic in-memory policy evaluator with typed errors and no side effects, provider clients, listener mutation, or persistence.
Deny-by-default routing is explicit: an unregistered method/path or missing route scope fails closed.
The slice moves cloud readiness from a broad missing-auth blocker to a tested local authorization foundation plus a narrower external identity-provider verification blocker.
The cloud-readiness gate now composes auth runtime readiness while cloud deployment remains false.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if cross-tenant requests, expired sessions, bad issuer/audience/nonce, unknown routes, missing scopes, weak assurance, missing MFA, break-glass misuse, or runtime-attachment overclaims are accepted.
findings: Positive route authorization and negative security-path coverage are both present.
Developers can call enterprise_auth_runtime_policy(), validate_enterprise_auth_runtime_policy(), and authorize_enterprise_route() to understand the pre-cloud auth boundary.

Targeted auth runtime check/test/clippy, cloud-readiness test/clippy, 37-package enterprise regression test/clippy, fmt, jq, data_class scan, quality-marker scan, dependency-seam gate, Oya VCS lifecycle, and audit-chain append-only checks are required for closeout.

alternatives_named: wire auth directly into existing preview route handlers
wait for a full external OIDC/JWKS gateway before adding auth semantics
add a local route-policy auth runtime and keep provider/gateway verification as a blocker
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A separate local runtime establishes route, tenant, scope, MFA, and break-glass semantics without falsely claiming cryptographic token verification or deployed gateway enforcement.
rejected_reasons: Direct route-handler mutation would imply enforcement on preview handlers that still explicitly lack a deployed listener.
Waiting for cloud gateway integration would leave local route security semantics untyped and untested.

findings: Authorization denies by default, enforces tenant isolation, validates issuer/audience/nonce/session boundaries, and requires route scopes.
Sensitive HR/payroll/accounting/suite routes require AAL2 and MFA; break-glass access requires audit marking.
The runtime refuses overclaims for external identity provider, JWKS, OIDC signature verification, durable sessions, deployed gateway, and runtime audit emission.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Authorization scans a fixed 19-route vector and checks scalar claim fields; no network, storage, cryptography, or hot listener path exists.

findings.summary: The foundation is bounded by the local route catalog and does not affect deployed traffic throughput because no deployed gateway is attached.

findings: All new public struct fields in changed source carry data_class annotations.

The design follows official OIDC/OAuth/NIST/OWASP themes by modeling issuer/audience/nonce/session checks, deny-by-default access control, least privilege route scopes, MFA/assurance for sensitive routes, and explicit external-provider verification as a later blocker.
The change is additive: one crate, one catalog row, spec/task/evidence updates, and readiness-gate composition. No migration, credential, or external resource is created.
Auth decisions surface audit_required and external_identity_verification_required flags for later runtime/gateway observability.
Runtime audit-chain emission remains an explicit non-claim and blocker.
Enterprise Suite AC-17 records the staged migration boundary from local auth semantics to later OIDC/JWKS/provider and deployed gateway enforcement.
AC-15 cloud-readiness wording now narrows the auth blocker to external identity-provider verification.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: A local auth runtime foundation can improve cloud readiness without claiming production authentication only if it refuses provider, signature-verification, durable-session, gateway, and runtime-audit overclaims.
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: The Enterprise Suite cloud gate would keep a broad auth-missing blocker with no tested route/tenant/scope semantics for later gateway work.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Existing preview route handlers intentionally do not enforce auth; a separate runtime-policy crate preserves their non-claim while enabling later gateway composition.

findings: This is the next cloud-integration step after deployment manifest foundation: route authorization semantics are now typed before listener/gateway deployment.
Names use auth-runtime-foundation vocabulary and avoid deployed-gateway or production-auth claims.
Enterprise Suite spec, plan, task list, catalog, multispectrum evidence, VCS evidence, and audit-chain references are part of the closeout set.
The crate sits under microservices/enterprise-suite/crates with a runtime-security catalog row and no new external service adapter.
No listener, route-handler mutation, durable store, provider SDK, JWKS fetcher, Workflow engine/broker, statutory rail, or runtime audit emitter was introduced.
The new auth runtime crate has no third-party dependencies; the readiness gate adds only a local workspace dependency on it.
No external wire API schema changes; the addition is a Rust control-plane/runtime-policy struct set plus Enterprise Suite AC-17 metadata.
Authorization is deterministic scalar/ref checking over the fixed route policy vector with no clock source, randomness, I/O, network, or provider calls.
